doc.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

title: Salary, royalties and the first Roberta Flack deal
summary: Dorn began at Atlantic on $250 a week, had an offer from Blue Note, and negotiated royalties the same week he made the first Roberta Flack record.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did the amount of records that sold make a difference in your income?
Not — because after about the first year I was on a royalty basis.
And I still get royalties off those records you know.
So you had a sort of a base salary and then —

I started at Atlantic for $250 a week. I took home $197. My records started coming out and I got pretty lucky pretty early. The stuff started selling so I renegotiated a contact about a year later. Because I actually had an offer from Blue Note at that time to go over there. And then I had a pretty good couple of years, another year as a salary, but Les McCann turned me on to Roberta Flack and I negotiated my first deal with royalties the same week I made the first Roberta Flack record which went on to sell four million pieces.
But I didn’t do it because I was smart, I did it because I said oh let me see if they’ll give me a royalty. You know, Mr. Simpson.
